question: After 1500 cycles, what capacity does the cathode deliver per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, and what sulfur share of the electrode does their ratio imply, against the sulfur content the paper states?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text, strength FROM atoms WHERE text ILIKE '%1500%' OR text ILIKE '%mAh%' OR text ILIKE '%wt%' OR text ILIKE '%loading%' OR text ILIKE '%mg cm%' OR text ILIKE '%sulfur content%' OR text ILIKE '%per gram%' OR text ILIKE '%g-1%' OR text ILIKE '%g−1%' ORDER BY page, top
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page=5 AND line_no BETWEEN 95 AND 115 OR (page=5 AND id IN ('p5.L103','p5.L104','p5.L105','p5.L106','p5.L107','p5.L108','p5.L109')) ORDER BY page, line_no

SELECT 100.0 * CAST(regexp_extract(b.text,'(\d+) mAh/g',1) AS DOUBLE) / CAST(regexp_extract(a.text,'(\d+) mAh/',1) AS DOUBLE) AS implied_sulfur_pct, CAST(regexp_extract(c.text,'(\d+) wt %',1) AS DOUBLE) AS stated_sulfur_pct, CAST(regexp_extract(a.text,'(\d+) mAh/',1) AS DOUBLE) AS per_gS, CAST(regexp_extract(b.text,'(\d+) mAh/g',1) AS DOUBLE) AS per_electrode FROM atoms a, atoms b, atoms c WHERE a.id='p5.L103' AND b.id='p5.L105' AND c.id='p5.L108'

rendered: After the initial decay, the higher-rate cathode test reports a capacity of 306 mAh/gS delivered at cycle 1500[1]. With respect to the entire electrode mass, the paper reports 87 mAh/g[2] after 1500 cycles[3]. Dividing the electrode-basis value by the sulfur-basis value gives an implied sulfur share of about 28.4[4] percent of the electrode. The paper itself states a moderate loading of 35 wt % active sulfur[5], so the implied share is noticeably lower than the stated sulfur content. The paper does not reconcile these sets of figures; the gap suggests the electrode mass includes substantial non-sulfur material beyond the sulfur-carbon composite, or that the values refer to different test conditions.
